captions.detailed: This 3D model is a multi-part toy double-decker bus designed for assembly. It consists of three main components: a hollow bus body shell, a flat chassis base, and four small cylindrical wheels with central axle holes. The bus body features rounded corners, horizontal trim ribs running along its exterior, two rows of rectangular windows representing the double-decker layout, wheel well cutouts, and internal clip-mounting structures. The separate flat chassis plate is shaped to fit snugly into the bottom of the shell and includes four raised axle pillow blocks to hold the wheel axles.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric toy double-decker bus in OpenSCAD that can be printed in separate parts. The script must include customizable parameters for overall length, width, height, shell thickness, window dimensions, wheel diameter, and chassis clip tolerances, and it should generate the hollow bus body, a snap-fit chassis base with axle pillow blocks, and four individual wheels.
captions.factory: The script is structured into modular components including body(), base(), wheel(), axleClip(), and baseClip(). The body module uses a hollowed-out rounded shell created by subtracting a scaled-down shell() from an outer shell(), with windows and wheel wells subtracted using difference() with cubes and cylinders. The base module uses a hull() over four corner cylinders to form a flat plate, with wheel well slots subtracted and axle clips unioned on top. The wheels are simple difference() cylinders with central axle holes, and the snap-fit baseClip() uses a linear_extrude() of a 2D polygon to create the latching profile.
